PIE word *h₁en Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₁énder. Proto-Slavic *vъ(n) Old East Slavic въ (vŭ) Russian в Inherited from Old East Slavic въ (vŭ), from Proto-Slavic *vъ(n), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁n̥, zero-grade form of *h₁én.

ety.text: Calque of French inclure or German einschließen, ultimately a calque of Latin inclūdō. By surface analysis, в- (v-) + -ключа́ть (-ključátʹ).
Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic въспльнити (vŭsplĭniti). By surface analysis, вос- (vos-) + -по́лнить (-pólnitʹ).

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *tỳsęťa, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tū́ˀsantis, from Proto-Indo-European *tuHsont-. Cognate with Ukrainian тисяча (tysjača), Serbo-Croatian тисућа, tisuća, Slovene tisoč, Czech and Slovak tisíc, Polish tysiąc. Akin to English thousand, Gothic 𐌸𐌿𐍃𐌿𐌽𐌳𐌹 (þūsundi), Lithuanian tūkstantis, Latvian tūkstotis.
